chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abd al-Karim ibn Utba who said:

I asked the Shaykh about a man who wakes up from his sleep and did not urinate — can he put his hand into the vessel before washing it? He said: No, because he does not know where his hand was, so let him wash it first.

key_terms.الإناء: The vessel/container used for water in ritual purification (wudu or ghusl)
key_terms.الشيخ: The Shaykh — a respectful title used for the Imam, here likely Imam al-Sadiq (AS)
key_terms.لا يدري: He does not know — the epistemic uncertainty that triggers the ruling
key_terms.يده: His hand — the instrument of potential impurity transfer

ai.seo_question: Can a man put his hand in a water vessel before washing it after waking from sleep in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith records a question posed by Abd al-Karim ibn Utba to the Imam (referred to as 'the Shaykh'), asking whether a man who wakes from sleep without urinating may dip his hand into a water vessel before washing it. The Imam rules that he may not, giving the legal rationale that the sleeper does not know where his hand was during sleep, meaning it may have come into contact with impurity. This establishes the precautionary principle in ritual purity law: uncertainty about potential najasah requires washing before contact with water vessels.
